implementation_notes: Declare an interface whose methods are suspend functions with Retrofit annotations; Retrofit generates the implementation proxy over OkHttp, so the delegate the client injects is generated and the interceptor chain carries auth headers, logging and retry policy. What replaces the classic structure: the lookup role is the Retrofit base URL plus discovery, and exception translation is mapping HttpException/IOException into a sealed Result in one wrapper. Hand-write the wrapper when responses need aggregation or domain mapping beyond DTO decoding.
code_sketch:
interface BillingApi {                       // local-looking delegate
    @POST("invoices") suspend fun createInvoice(@Body cmd: CreateInvoice): Invoice
}
// Retrofit generates the implementation over OkHttp:
val api = Retrofit.Builder()
    .baseUrl(BASE_URL)
    .addConverterFactory(MoshiConverterFactory.create())
    .client(okHttpWithAuth)
    .build()
    .create(BillingApi::class.java)
val invoice = api.createInvoice(cmd)         // suspends, caller thread not blocked
pitfalls: suspend functions throw HttpException/IOException; if call sites must not see Retrofit types, translate once into a sealed result.
OkHttpClient is expensive and must be shared; building Retrofit per call leaks connection and thread pools.
Retrofit is JVM/Android-only - a Kotlin Multiplatform module cannot use it.
A blocking interceptor still occupies an OkHttp dispatcher thread even though the caller is suspending.

variants.name: Ktor HttpClient wrapper (multiplatform, coroutine-first)
variants.idiom_name: HttpClient + suspend wrapper class using the request DSL
variants.implementation_notes: No proxy generation: a class wraps one configured Ktor HttpClient and exposes suspend functions that build requests with the DSL (client.post + content negotiation), and the wrapper maps ResponseException/IOException into a domain Result. Choose it for Kotlin Multiplatform or non-Android services where Retrofit's JVM-only proxy is unavailable; keep request building inside the wrapper so the rest of the application never imports Ktor types.
pitfalls: HttpClient must be shared and closed; creating one per call leaks the connection pool and dispatcher threads.
ResponseException, HttpRequestTimeoutException and serialization failures are distinct classes - translate all of them or callers see serialization errors as network errors.
HttpTimeout is plugin-configured and off by default, so hung calls block until the platform timeout.
